statuses.title: Identify assistant spans correctly in Gemma chat templates
statuses.note: The silent whole-template-wrap fallback (which flagged user tokens as assistant tokens) is gone: every strategy's output must pass _generation_block_marks_only_assistant (renders user/assistant probes and requires assistant-probe-in / user-probe-out, _chat_template.py:422-445), and failure raises ValueError instead of guessing (256-261). Probed with real templates: Gemma-2 produces exactly the '<start_of_turn>model\n...<end_of_turn>\n' spans; Qwen2.5-Instruct correct; real Gemma-3, Llama-3-Instruct, and canonical shared-expression ChatML fail closed with ValueError (safe, never silently wrong). Caveats reported as a finding: internal comments overstate coverage and the exact-string '{% generation %}' guards mishandle whitespace-control marker variants that HF itself accepts.

statuses.title: Preserve policy adapters when a PEFT reference model is supplied
statuses.note: null_ref_context now treats ANY non-None ref_model as separate (no-op; no adapter toggling on the policy) and rejects ref_model is model with ValueError before mutating anything (_adapter.py:152-163). Trainer call sites match: explicit ref (PEFT or not) is used directly with null_ref=False; only the no-ref PEFT case toggles the policy's adapter (_dpo_trainer.py:635-660, 737-742). Regression tests test_separate_peft_reference_path_leaves_policy_adapter_active and test_shared_peft_reference_model_is_rejected_before_mutating_policy pass with real peft LoRA models.

statuses.title: Validate alignment losses with locality and independent parity tests
statuses.note: tests/test_row_locality.py NaN-poisons one row and asserts every other row's forward value and vmap(grad) per-example gradient are untouched, parametrized over the full public __all__ of dpo.loss + sft.loss with a hard pytest.fail for any unregistered export (closes the OPQ-154 gap, including bco/ipo/simpo/apo/exo/sppo/odds_ratio and all combinators, plus per-example lm_head gradient slices for the fused losses). tests/test_trl_parity.py executes real TRL (DPO inline loss, CPO, ORPO, dft_loss) — value, mean, and gradient. All pass locally. Caveat reported as a finding: the suite exposed that wpo_weights does NOT match TRL/the WPO paper and left it as a strict xfail rather than fixing it.

statuses.title: Include reference-model identity in DPO cache fingerprints
statuses.note: cache_identity is now a required kwarg of compute_ref_logprobs_for_dataset; the fingerprint is SHA-256 over a versioned canonical JSON of (dataset._fingerprint, cache_identity, output_columns) with _CACHE_FINGERPRINT_VERSION=2 invalidating pre-fix caches, and non-JSON identities raise TypeError instead of falling back to repr (_precompute.py:97-153). The DPO trainer supplies _model_cache_identity: a SHA-256 over the reference's full state_dict bytes+dtypes+shapes, with adapter_mode and (for active-PEFT refs) live adapter status; the PEFT null-ref case excludes adapter tensors so the digest matches the effective base-only reference (_dpo_trainer.py:151-211, 661-664). Distinct refs can no longer alias one cache entry.

statuses.title: Shard reference-logprob precomputation across ranks
statuses.note: Each rank scores a contiguous local_shard slice (engine _shard.py:52-55) and shards are re-concatenated in rank order via one all_gather_object-based gather_pytree (engine _state.py:300-314, _merge_gathered_pytrees preserves rank order), reproducing single-process order; per-column row counts are validated against len(dataset) (_precompute.py:325-333). Collective symmetry holds: dataset size and _fingerprint are asserted equal across ranks up front, the cache-hit decision is min-reduced unconditionally before any early return, empty shards contribute None but still join the collective, and only main writes the cache before wait_for_everyone (_precompute.py:405-460). tests/ddp/test_precompute_shard.py (2-rank Gloo) passes locally.

findings.title: wpo_weights omits the WPO paper's per-token alignment term (and thus disagrees with TRL)
findings.claim: With DPOConfig(use_weighting=True), opaque's WPO pair weight is exp(mean masked per_token_logps) while both the cited WPO paper (arXiv:2406.11827, Eq. 2) and TRL 1.12 subtract the per-token alignment term log(sum_v p(v)^2) before averaging; the trainer multiplies per-example losses by this wrong weight, so WPO runs optimize a different objective than the paper the docstring claims to implement. The repo knows: test_trl_parity.py:518-526 marks the parity test as strict xfail instead of fixing the weight. Possibly inside the umbrella of OPEN issue #323 ('align trainer and alignment behavior with their public contracts'), but no open issue names WPO specifically.
findings.failure_scenario: User sets use_weighting=True (WPO) on DPOTrainer expecting the published WPO objective / TRL-equivalent behavior. _dpo_trainer.py:1139-1144 multiplies each pair's loss by _wpo_weight(chosen)*_wpo_weight(rejected) built from raw per-token logps; TRL computes aligned_logps = per_token_logps - (logsumexp(2x) - 2*logsumexp(x)) first (site-packages/trl/trainer/dpo_trainer.py:1595-1606). Since log(sum p^2) is in [-log V, 0] and varies per token, the two weights differ systematically (opaque's are smaller and differently ranked), silently changing training dynamics and results versus the cited method.
evidence: packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/dpo/loss/_wpo.py:62-67 — 'avg_logp = (per_token_logps * mask).to(acc_dtype).sum(dim=-1); avg_logp = avg_logp / token_count...; return avg_logp.detach().exp()' — no logits, no alignment term.

packages/opaque-alignment/tests/test_trl_parity.py:518-526 — '@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=("wpo_weights omits the WPO weight-alignment term log(sum_v p_v^2) that both TRL and the authors' reference implementation apply; the fix needs the logits, so it changes the public signature"))'.

.venv trl 1.12.0 dpo_trainer.py:1595-1606 — 'lse2 = torch.logsumexp(2.0 * shift_logits, dim=-1); log_denom = lse2 - 2.0 * lse1; aligned_logps = (per_token_logps - log_denom) * shift_completion_mask; ... weights = torch.exp(mean_logps)'.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_dpo_trainer.py:1139-1144 applies the product of the two opaque weights to the per-example loss; the trainer's _wpo_weight already receives chosen_out.logits, so the logits needed for the fix are available at that call site.
findings.fix_sketch: Add an optional logits (or log_denom) argument to wpo_weights and compute avg over (per_token_logps - (logsumexp(2*logits,-1) - 2*logsumexp(logits,-1))) under no_grad, mirroring TRL; wire _dpo_trainer._wpo_weight to pass the logits it already has; flip the xfail into a passing parity test. The weight stays detached and per-example, so DP clipping semantics are unchanged.

findings.title: Docs still advertise the deleted SquareChiPO head as implemented
findings.claim: Commit 17c58f8c (issue #393) deleted the non-private SquareChiPO loss, but docs/alignment/dpo.md:46 and docs/alignment/trainers.md:18 still list SquareChiPO among 'Implemented preference heads' / 'supported loss_type values', and docs/reference/alignment.md:78 keeps it in the implemented-loss citation list — advertising a differentially-private-PO method (the paper's title says 'Differentially Private') that the library no longer ships.

Construction fails with an unknown-loss KeyError (_dpo_trainer.py:349-353) — fail-loud, so no silent harm, but the docs promise a privacy-relevant capability that does not exist.
evidence: docs/alignment/trainers.md:13-20 — 'The supported loss_type values map onto the corresponding alignment papers: ... [SquareChiPO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.21395) ...'.
docs/alignment/dpo.md:41-48 — 'Implemented preference heads in this guide follow the primary papers for ... [SquareChiPO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.21395) ...'.
docs/reference/alignment.md:78 — SquareChiPO citation row still present.
grep -rni squarechipo packages/ --include='*.py' returns nothing; git show 17c58f8c removed _squarechipo.py and tests/dpo/loss/test_squarechipo.py.

findings.title: Chat-template transform: overstated coverage comments and exact-string generation-marker guards
findings.claim: Residuals around the #387 fix (all fail-closed, none silently wrong): (a) the Strategy-2 comment 'Handles ChatML, Llama-3, Phi-3, etc.' (line 229) and the _wrap_gemma_shared_expression docstring 'Gemma 2/3 templates' (line 376) overstate coverage — the real Llama-3-Instruct template, canonical shared-expression ChatML, and the real Gemma-3 text template all raise ValueError (Gemma-3 because its '{{ raise_exception("Invalid content type") }}' expression matches the \bcontent\b regex, making content_matches count 2 and aborting at line 405); (b) both the idempotency check (line 214, '_GEN_START in template') and apply_chat_template_with_mask's guard (_completion_mask.py:84, exact "{% generation %}" substring) miss whitespace-control marker variants ('{%- generation -%}') that transformers itself accepts via regex, so a valid pre-marked template is either rejected outright or gets a second nested marker pair (verified: nesting yields duplicated identical spans, so the final mask is still correct).
findings.failure_scenario: SFTTrainer with completion_only_loss on chat data and a Llama-3/ChatML/Gemma-3 tokenizer raises ValueError at dataset prep despite comments suggesting support; a user who hand-installed '{%- generation -%}' markers (valid per transformers' r"\{\%-?\s*generation\s*-?\%\}" check, chat_template_utils) gets a ValueError from apply_chat_template_with_mask telling them to install markers they already have. Training either stops with a confusing error or proceeds correctly after redundant re-wrapping — no wrong mask is ever produced.
evidence: Probe run against real templates: GEMMA2 spans ['<start_of_turn>model\nASSIST1<end_of_turn>\n', ...] correct; GEMMA3, CHATML (shared-expression), LLAMA3 all 'ValueError (fail-closed)'; QWEN25 correct.

_chat_template.py:403-406 — content_pat matches both "{{ message['content'] | trim }}" and '{{ raise_exception("Invalid content type") }}' in the real Gemma-3 template (probe printed both), so len(content_matches) != 1 returns None.

_completion_mask.py:84 — 'if not active_template or "{% generation %}" not in active_template: raise ValueError' vs transformers 5.16.1 chat_template_utils: 'if return_assistant_tokens_mask and not re.search(r"\{\%-?\s*generation\s*-?\%\}", chat_template)'.

Probe: get_training_chat_template on a template already containing '{%- generation -%}' returned a nested '{%- generation -%}{% generation %}...{% endgeneration %}{%- endgeneration -%}' template; rendered indices [(26, 41), (26, 41)] — duplicated but identical spans.
findings.fix_sketch: Use the same whitespace-tolerant regex as transformers for both the idempotency check and the _completion_mask guard; fix the Strategy-2 comment to name templates it actually handles (role-branched templates, Phi-3) and drop 'Gemma 3' from the helper docstring, or exclude raise_exception(...) expressions from content_pat so real Gemma-3 works.

findings.title: DiscoPOP module cites a fabricated author/title; sequence_logp docstring denies the ld_alpha feature it implements
findings.claim: Two doc inaccuracies that survived the citation-repair commit 1d216fcd (#503): (a) _discopop.py:5-7 (and discopop_loss's docstring line 41) attribute DiscoPOP to 'Azar, M. G., et al. (2024). DiscoPOP: Discovering Preference Optimization Procedures Using Self-Supervised Feedback. NeurIPS 2024' — a nonexistent citation; the actual paper is Lu et al., 'Discovering Preference Optimization Algorithms with and for Large Language Models' (arXiv:2406.08414), which docs/reference/alignment.md:72 cites correctly, and Azar et al. is the IPO paper; (b) logprob/_sequence.py:15-16 module docstring says the ld_alpha LD-DPO split 'is not implemented here; pass ld_alpha=None' while sequence_logp in the same file fully implements ld_alpha (lines 81-100) and its own function docstring documents it — the only true limitation is on fused_sequence_logp.
findings.failure_scenario: The project's own DP review protocol requires verifying mathematical claims against primary sources and forbids invented citations; a reviewer or user following _discopop.py's reference cannot find the paper (wrong author, wrong subtitle) and may mis-verify the formula against Azar et al. (IPO). A caller reading _sequence.py's module docstring concludes ld_alpha is unsupported and builds a manual LD-DPO path unnecessarily, or distrusts the trainer's ld_alpha wiring.
evidence: _discopop.py:5-7 — 'Azar, M. G., et al. (2024). DiscoPOP: Discovering Preference Optimization Procedures Using Self-Supervised Feedback. NeurIPS 2024.'

docs/reference/alignment.md:72 — 'DiscoPOP — Lu et al., *Discovering Preference Optimization Algorithms with and for Large Language Models* (https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.08414)' (the correct citation, showing the repo knows the right source).

logprob/_sequence.py:15-16 — 'The ``ld_alpha`` (LD-DPO, arXiv:2409.06411) length-desensitised logp split is not implemented here; pass ``ld_alpha=None``.' vs lines 81-100 implementing exactly that split ('if ld_alpha is not None: ... weight = target_weight * ld_weight').
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the _discopop.py citation with Lu et al., arXiv:2406.08414 (matching docs/reference/alignment.md); rewrite _sequence.py's module-docstring sentence to say the ld_alpha split IS implemented by sequence_logp and only the fused path lacks it.
